publisher: Bundesamt fuer Statistik (BFS / FSO, Swiss Federal Statistical Office), Schweizerische Lohnstrukturerhebung (LSE / Swiss Earnings Structure Survey) 2024
raw_extract:
BFS, Lohnstruktur (Earnings Structure): 'Sie erlaubt eine regelmaessige Beschreibung der schweizerischen Lohnstruktur auf der Basis repraesentativer Daten fuer saemtliche Wirtschaftszweige des sekundaeren und des tertiaeren Sektors in der Schweiz.'

VERBATIM: 'Im Jahr 2024 betrug der Medianlohn 7024 Franken brutto pro Monat. In der Schweiz gibt es nach wie vor grosse Lohnunterschiede je nach Wirtschaftsbranche und Profil der Arbeitnehmenden.'

VERBATIM (LSE method page / STAT-TAB definition, px-x-0304010000_205): 'Standardisierter Monatslohn: Vollzeitaequivalent basierend auf 4 1/3 Wochen a 40 Arbeitsstunden. Lohnkomponenten: Bruttolohn im Monat Oktober (inkl. Arbeitnehmerbeitraege an die Sozialversicherung, Naturalleistungen, regelmaessig ausbezahlte Praemien-, Umsatz- oder Provisionsanteile), Entschädigung fuer Schicht-, Nacht- und Sonntagsarbeit, 1/12 vom 13. Monatslohn und 1/12 von den jaehrlichen Sonderzahlungen. Nicht beruecksichtigt werden die Familienzulagen und die Kinderzulagen. Privater und oeffentlicher Sektor zusammen, in Franken.'

VERBATIM (BFS Medienmitteilung, 25.11.2025, admin.ch): 'Im Jahr 2024 belief sich der monatliche Bruttomedianlohn fuer eine Vollzeitstelle (privater und oeffentlicher Sektor zusammen) auf 7024 Franken pro Monat (2022: 6788 Franken). Die 10% der Arbeitnehmenden mit den tiefsten Loehnen verdienten weniger als 4635 Franken pro Monat, waehrend die am besten bezahlten 10% der Arbeitnehmenden einen Lohn von ueber 12 526 Franken erhielten.'

VERBATIM (BFS, Monatlicher Bruttolohn nach Beruflicher Stellung und Geschlecht, 2024, Zentralwert (Median), in Franken, privater und oeffentlicher Sektor zusammen):
Total | 7 024 | 6 666 | 7 276
Berufliche Stellung 1+2 (top and upper management) | 11 174 | 10 077 | 11 715
3 (middle management) | 9 493 | 8 915 | 9 856
4 (supervisory / lower management) | 7 740 | 7 424 | 7 949
5 (employees without management responsibility) | 6 368 | 6 160 | 6 499

VERBATIM (BFS, Monatlicher Bruttolohn nach Grossregionen und beruflicher Stellung, 2024, Median, in Franken):
Genferseeregion 6 998 | Espace Mittelland 6 964 | Nordwestschweiz 7 156 | Zuerich 7 502 | Ostschweiz 6 623 | Zentralschweiz 7 092 | Tessin 5 708 | Schweiz 7 024

claims.statement: VERBATIM: 'Im Jahr 2024 betrug der Medianlohn 7024 Franken brutto pro Monat.' Median standardised GROSS monthly wage for a full-time post (100%) in the Swiss economy as a whole, private and public sector combined, from the Swiss Earnings Structure Survey 2024. Expressed by the BFS as CHF 84 288 per year on a 12x basis, or CHF 91 312 on the Swiss conventional 13x basis.

VERBATIM table row 5: employees WITHOUT management responsibility (Berufliche Stellung 5), median gross monthly wage, men and women combined, Switzerland 2024 = CHF 6 368. This is the closest published bracket to the situation of a new graduate, who will not be a manager.

VERBATIM regional table: Canton Ticino (Tessin), all professional positions, median gross monthly wage 2024 = CHF 5 708, the lowest of the seven Swiss gross regions. Zurich is CHF 7 502. Recorded to make the size of the regional spread explicit.
VERBATIM: 'Die 10% der Arbeitnehmenden mit den tiefsten Loehnen verdienten weniger als 4635 Franken pro Monat.' The 10th percentile (Tieflohn) gross monthly wage threshold, Switzerland 2024.
VERBATIM: 'waehrend die am besten bezahlten 10% der Arbeitnehmenden einen Lohn von ueber 12 526 Franken erhielten.' The 90th percentile gross monthly wage threshold, Switzerland 2024.

assumptions: SOURCE'S OWN: 'Standardisierter Monatslohn' is a full-time-equivalent standardised monthly wage based on 4 1/3 weeks of 40 hours per week, so the figure is already normalised for part-time workers rather than being a simple average of what people are actually paid.

SOURCE'S OWN: the wage components INCLUDE the employee's social insurance contributions, benefits in kind, regularly paid premium/commission/turnover shares, shift/night/Sunday allowances, 1/12 of the 13th month's wage and 1/12 of annual special payments. This is what 'brutto' means here.
SOURCE'S OWN: family allowances and child allowances are NOT included.
SOURCE'S OWN: private and public sector combined; Switzerland only; full-time posts; reference month October of the even-numbered survey year.
NOT THE SOURCE'S / MINE: nothing was deducted from these figures and no net figure was constructed from them in this artifact.
NOT THE SOURCE'S / MINE: no canton, occupation, age, sex, nationality or permit status was selected by me; the headline figures are national totals.
NOT THE SOURCE'S / MINE: no FX conversion and no PPP factor. CHF is the reporting currency.
notes: *** THIS IS GROSS, NOT NET. *** CHF 7 024 per month is Swiss pay BEFORE the employee share of AHV/IV/EO (5.3 per cent), ALV (1.1 per cent), non-occupational accident insurance NBU, occupational pension BVG, and BEFORE federal, cantonal and municipal income tax. A new graduate would in practice be nearer the CHF 6 368 'no management responsibility' figure than the CHF 7 024 headline. Switzerland-specific warning that a reader would be misled by: the BFS figure includes 1/12 of the 13th month's wage and 1/12 of annual special payments, so on the Swiss conventional 13-times-annual reckoning the annualised headline is CHF 91 312, not CHF 84 288; dividing by 12 or by 13 without stating the convention will produce different 'annual salary' numbers from the same published statistic. Also note the huge regional spread - CHF 5 708 in Ticino versus CHF 7 502 in Zurich is a 31 per cent gap on gross alone, before cantonal tax rates, so a single national CHF figure is a poor basis for a break-even calculation without a canton. The corresponding net evidence for Switzerland is weak; see artifacts 020_net_monthly_income.json and 030_raw_status_net_monthly_income.json. Currency CHF, reference year 2024, first results published 25 November 2025.
evidence_limitations: All occupations and all ages pooled, so it includes long-tenured senior staff who pull the median far above an entry-level salary. Median, not mean. Full-time-equivalent, not actual pay received. October reference month, so it is seasonally unrepresentative for some sectors. Gross only - the BFS publishes no national net median. No graduate-specific breakdown was located in the accessible BFS outputs; the LSE does break wages down by education level ('universitaere Hochschule (UNI, ETH)' versus 'Fachhochschule (FH, PH)' versus 'EFZ') but only in the gross tables reached here.
